sources.entry: Tietie - Open-source clipboard history for Mac and Windows with number-key pasting and search for text inside images, with an interface in Traditional Chinese. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/KLWSharpe/tietie) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Tietie (貼貼) is a free, open-source clipboard history manager for Mac and Windows that records text, images and files and lets you paste past items by number key, with OCR-based image search.
summary.what_it_does: Tietie records text, images, and files that you copy, keeping up to 1000 items by default (images capped at 2 GB). Pressing a global shortcut (Shift+Command+V on Mac, Ctrl+Shift+V on Windows) opens the list, where items are numbered so pressing 1–9 or 0 pastes that entry. Typing searches the history, including text recognized inside copied images. Items can be pinned so they survive history clearing, and the last 10 minutes or the full history can be cleared from the menu. Images can be pasted as their extracted text, and pasted text drops its original formatting. All records are stored locally, and the app only contacts GitHub to check for updates. The interface supports seven languages, including Traditional Chinese and English.
use_cases: keep a history of recently copied text and images
paste an earlier copied item quickly by number
find a copied snippet or screenshot by searching its text
paste the text inside a screenshot as plain text
clear sensitive copied content after use
replace Clipy on newer macOS versions
how_to_run: Mac: run the one-line curl installer shown in the README in Terminal (requires macOS 13 or later).
Windows: run the one-line irm | iex installer in PowerShell (Windows 10 or 11).
Build from source on Mac: install Xcode Command Line Tools, clone the repo, then run ./scripts/build.sh; the app is output to build/Tietie.app.
Build Windows from source: install the .NET 8 SDK and run dotnet publish on windows/Tietie/Tietie.csproj with -r win-x64.
notable: Number-key paste: each history row is numbered, and pressing 1–9 or 0 pastes that item directly
Searches text inside copied images, and can paste the recognized text instead of the image
Records text, images, and files; file entries store only the path, so moved or deleted originals cannot be pasted
Fully local storage with no record uploads; the only network call checks GitHub for new versions
Interface available in seven languages with automatic language detection and manual switching
caveats: On Mac, auto-paste requires granting Accessibility permission, and it must be re-granted through the app menu after each update because the app is not signed with a paid Apple developer account
Records are not encrypted; anyone with access to the computer can read them, so the README suggests disabling password-manager capture on shared machines
File history entries break if the original file is moved or deleted
Windows support is described with a separate install guide and Windows-specific shortcut mapping (Ctrl instead of Command, Alt instead of Option)
